extracted.intended_audience: screenwriters, novelists, playwrights, and storytellers studying narrative craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and structural criteria for creating compelling narratives across screen, page, and stage, with emphasis on form, character, antagonism, and dramatic turning points. Useful for writers learning classical and alternative story structures and scene-level mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form over formula (Core Premise)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Story is about form, not formula."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize architectural principles common to compelling narrative rather than slavish adherence to a prescriptive template. Understand functional dramatic form so you can apply it flexibly across mediums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical design: active protagonist, external conflict, closed ending, linear time, causality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most great commercial work sits in archplot. Use a clear protagonist driving action against external antagonism, maintain causal chain and momentum toward a resolved ending; deviating risks confusing audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miniplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimalist: subtle, internal, open-ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often used in literary work. Emphasize interior life, internal conflict, and ambiguity in resolution; accept less overt external causality and more open endings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antiplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-structure: coincidence, nonlinear, inconsistent reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subverts conventional structure; can be used artistically but typically sits outside mainstream commercial expectations. Use deliberately and with awareness of how it alters audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-Part Structure (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: A structural arc broken into five linked story phases that drive dramatic causality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the five parts as an organizing spine so each story event builds toward the climax; each phase has distinct purpose and must flow causally into the next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inciting incident
rubrics_metrics.description: The event that throws the protagonist's life out of balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must alter the protagonist's condition and trigger pursuit of the object of desire; should be early and clearly motivate subsequent action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive complications
rubrics_metrics.description: Escalating obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obstacles should increase stakes and difficulty in a causal, escalating manner. Avoid static or repetitive challenges; each complication should deepen conflict and force change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision point with greatest pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The protagonist faces a crucial choice (not merely an event). The crisis tests values and priorities and leads directly to the climactic action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision/action that resolves the conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The whole story exists for the climax. Everything else must build to and justify this moment; it should be the inevitable result of choices under pressure and the turning of story values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Aftermath; new equilibrium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show consequences and establish a new status quo that reflects the protagonist's choices. Closure should feel earned by the climax and not be tacked on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Want vs. Need
rubrics_metrics.description: Conscious desire (want) vs. unconscious desire (need).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate what the protagonist thinks they want from what they truly need; use dramatic events to reveal the conflict between the two and drive internal arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object of Desire
rubrics_metrics.description: What the protagonist consciously seeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The object should be concrete and drive plot; it focuses action and reveals character through pursuit. Ensure the object is tied to deeper needs for thematic resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forces of Antagonism
rubrics_metrics.description: The sum of all forces opposing the protagonist's will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antagonism includes people, society, nature, fate, and inner conflicts; the story's power correlates with the quality, variety, and escalation of these opposing forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of Antagonism
rubrics_metrics.description: A protagonist and her story are compelling only to the degree antagonism makes them so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design antagonistic forces to test and reveal character; without credible opposition, choices are meaningless and drama collapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience expectations dictated by the chosen genre; subvert artfully, never ignore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the rules and expectations of your genre. You may subvert conventions, but do so deliberately and with respect for the audience's implicit contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Period, duration, location, level of conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use setting to shape possibility, constraint, and tone. Clear, coherent setting choices influence stakes and plausibility of actions and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Values (scene-level criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every scene must turn on a story value (life/death, love/hate, freedom/oppression, etc.) and that value must shift positive↔negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign a clear charged value to each scene and ensure the scene produces a measurable shift in that value; scenes that don't change value fail dramatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat
rubrics_metrics.description: Smallest unit; an exchange of behavior in action/reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose scenes from beats; each beat advances pressure, reveals character, or turns value. Beats should be sharply defined and causal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene
rubrics_metrics.description: A story event that turns a value charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scenes must have a clear value at stake and end with a change in that value. Avoid filler scenes that do not alter the dramatic balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: 2–5 scenes, climaxing in significant turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group scenes into sequences that build toward a mini-climax or major turning point; sequences organize pacing and escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of sequences peaking in a major reversal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts mark major shifts in dramatic direction; each should culminate in a reversal that propels the next act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negation of the Negation
rubrics_metrics.description: Deeper stories descend past the simple negative to the contrary of the contrary (e.g., from hate to self-hatred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use layered value shifts to reveal deeper, darker dimensions of character and theme; this deepening helps achieve emotional and thematic complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization (observable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of observable qualities (job, age, appearance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, specific details to make characters believable, but remember that surface traits are not the same as moral or psychological truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: True Character (revealed under pressure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revealed only by choice under pressure; 'the deeper the pressure, the deeper the revelation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show who a character truly is through decisions in high-stakes situations rather than through static description; escalate pressure to reveal truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show, Don't Tell
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatize — don't narrate exposition. 'If a thing can be shown, it must be shown.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor action and interaction that reveal information organically. Use exposition sparingly and only where showing is impossible or would harm clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax as Storytelling's Soul
rubrics_metrics.description: The climax is the narrative's central purpose; the whole story exists for this moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure every element (beats, scenes, sequences, acts, character choices) to credibly produce and justify the climax; ensure the climax resolves the core value conflict.
